tos.title: Before you start
tos.p1: The app is free and has no ads. Microphone sound is processed on the device only and is never sent anywhere.
tos.p2: Everything you add yourself — recordings, tabs, lyrics — stays on your device and is your responsibility. Only add things you have the rights to.

stone.title: Stone
stone.path: travelled — how far a pebble rolls down a river to wear this smooth (50 m per hour of practice)
stone.text: An ordinary stone from the road. Every hour of practice in the app wears it down, like a stone kicked and rolled for years: sharp edges smooth out first (the first hundreds of hours), then chips and bumps go and it becomes a rounded version of itself (thousands of hours), and slowest of all it grows round — almost a ball after tens of thousands of hours. The stone can be turned with a finger.

help.listHint: An instruction opens by itself when its tool or section is opened — until “Don’t show again” is ticked. All of them are here.
hc.start.name: How Melete works
hc.start.what: Melete is a practice journal and a set of musician’s tools. Everything stays on this device, with no account and no ads.
hc.start.1: “Practice” is the week: how much of the goal is done, practice days, the stone that is polished by practice hours, and Melete with the word of the day.
hc.start.2: “Start practice” begins a session: time runs by itself, and tools open as windows right inside it.
hc.start.3: “Songs” holds songs with key, tempo, lyrics and chords, tabs and recordings; “Calendar” holds rehearsals, lessons and concerts.
hc.start.4: “Tools” — metronome, tuner, piano, pads, theory, recorder and more; each also opens without a session.
hc.start.5: The profile (top-left icon) — goal, notifications and Melete’s character, appearance, data, the Melete folder and these instructions.
hc.start.tip: The rhythm is weekly: a missed day resets nothing. The week matters, not a streak of days.
hc.songs.name: Songs
hc.songs.what: A song library: everything needed to learn a song, in one card.
hc.songs.1: “+” adds a song: title, artist, key, target and current tempo, lyrics with chords ([Am] before a syllable or a chord line above the text).
hc.songs.2: Categories, genres and labels help find things; sorting by recency, mastery or time.
hc.songs.3: The song card shows time and sessions, a tempo chart and calendar events; “Play” starts a session with the song.
hc.songs.4: Tabs, scores and recordings are linked to the song and open in its session; lyrics and chords — in “Tabs and lyrics”.
hc.songs.5: The “Share” icon sends songs to the team in one file or receives a .melete file.
hc.songs.tip: Write lyrics with chords right away — transposition in “Tabs and lyrics” moves them to any key.
hc.session.name: Practice session
hc.session.what: A session is the practice itself: time runs, tools sit in windows, and there is a summary at the end.
hc.session.1: Tool windows can be dragged to swap places and resized (full, half, quarter, strip).
hc.session.2: Pause stops the time; the pomodoro in the header runs work and breaks, and the session pauses during a break.
hc.session.3: After a long time without sound or touches, the app asks whether practice is still going — to keep the time honest.
hc.session.4: The session can be minimized: time keeps running and the app works in the background while an instrument sounds.
hc.session.5: “Finish” asks for song mastery, a confident tempo and a note; the time goes into the week’s statistics.
hc.session.tip: A short session every day beats one long one at the weekend — the stone is polished by regularity.
hc.calendar.name: Calendar
hc.calendar.what: Rehearsals, lessons, concerts, recordings, deadlines and goals — in one calendar.
hc.calendar.1: “+” adds an event: type, time, repeat (daily, weekly, monthly, yearly), place, songs and a note.
hc.calendar.2: An event’s songs are a set list: from the event they can be sent to the team in one file.
hc.calendar.3: Deadlines and goals can be marked done; one occurrence of a repeating event can be removed.
hc.calendar.4: The “Share” icon at the top exports .ics for Google and other calendars.
hc.calendar.tip: Upcoming events also show on the home screen and in each song’s card.
hc.folder.name: Melete folder
hc.folder.what: A folder on the phone where all the data is sorted: visible in a file manager, ready to move, replace and add to.
hc.folder.1: Profile → Data and backups → Choose or create a folder: in the system picker (it opens Documents) create a Melete folder and allow access.
hc.folder.2: Data/melete-data.json is a copy of all data (songs, sessions, settings). Move it to a new phone and tap “Restore data from the folder”.
hc.folder.3: Media — recordings and video, Tabs — tabs and scores (Guitar Pro, MusicXML), PDF — scores and books, Lyrics — lyrics with chords (.cho).
hc.folder.4: Any file can simply be dropped into the folder or its root — the app finds and sorts it; a text file becomes a song.
hc.folder.5: Editing a song’s lyrics in its .cho file updates the song, editing in the app updates the file. Deleting a file from the folder deletes nothing in the app.
hc.folder.tip: Syncing happens at launch, on returning to the app and after changes; “Sync now” does it at once.
hc.share.name: Team: send and receive
hc.share.what: Songs, tabs and set lists go to team members in one .melete file — no servers, no sign-up.
hc.share.1: Songs → Share → Send songs: tick songs, optionally tabs, scores and recordings, then choose Telegram, WhatsApp or email.
hc.share.2: A rehearsal set list: open the event in the calendar → “Send to the team with songs” — the order, date and place go too.
hc.share.3: To receive: open the .melete file from the messenger in Melete, or Songs → Share → Receive a file.
hc.share.4: For each song — add, update the existing one or skip; a song sent again is updated, not duplicated.
hc.share.5: Personal data stays: mastery, difficulty, current tempo, labels and practice time remain each person’s own.
hc.share.tip: If the leader changes a key, just send the file again: everyone’s key updates and their mastery is kept.
hc.melete.name: Melete and reminders
hc.melete.what: Melete is the app’s mascot: on the home screen she shows the week’s mood and says one word a day; in notifications she reminds about practice.
hc.melete.1: Character: “Classic” — an hour and 5 minutes before practice; “Clingy” — all day; “Custom” — an own list; “No notifications” — silence.
hc.melete.2: Practice time, how early to remind and addressing by name — in Profile → Notifications.
hc.melete.3: Melete’s words come from the chosen sets: rock and jazz, classical, Bible, Christian writers, the book of wisdom; an own collection can be added.
hc.melete.4: Tapping Melete makes her react; her face follows the week: glad, happy, waiting, missing practice, asleep.
hc.melete.5: On a day with practice done, reminders stop; from 22:00 to 8:00 it is quiet.
hc.melete.6: If notifications don’t arrive, allow them in the phone settings and check with the “Test” button.
hc.melete.tip: Melete and the word of the day are turned off in Features; reminders — with the “No notifications” character.
hc.owndata.name: Own data and AI
hc.owndata.what: Own songs, quote collections and a profile can be loaded as one file — any AI chatbot can build it from the ready instructions.
hc.owndata.1: Profile → About me → Instructions for an AI: copy the text and give it to a chatbot with a request (“Sunday set list”, “quotes about hard work”).
hc.owndata.2: The chatbot returns a JSON file — save it as name.melete.json.
hc.owndata.3: “Load a file” — the app shows what’s inside (songs, collections, profile) and asks what to accept.
hc.owndata.4: Practice hours, statistics, experience, ranks and mastery can’t be changed by a file — only the app itself counts them.
hc.owndata.tip: Data can be loaded at the very first sign-up too — then the sign-up steps are already filled in.

guard.hint: On many phones a three-finger touch takes a screenshot, turning a chord on the piano or pads into a screenshot. While the piano, glider or pads are open, screenshots are blocked — and screen recording pauses too (this is how Android works). In other instruments and on all app screens screenshots and screen recording work. To record playing the piano, turn this protection off here. The gesture itself can also be turned off in the phone settings (Gestures → Three-finger screenshot).
